Been to prison. Cigs are the money. The value of cigs is totally dependent on whether tobacco is allowed at the facility. In facilities where tobacco is not allowed, the price of a cig goes to way up. My experience was somewhat unique to this discussion, because they disallowed tobacco during my tenure. Before the ban, the price of a pack (20 cigs) was about $1 on the commissary, and traded for about $1. Pot was quite expensive, at about $50 for a matchbox, or about 1.5 - 2 grams. After the ban on tobacco, a single cig would sell for about $5, so an inflation of 5000% from the pre-ban price. The pot price really never changed.

This, of course, is based on the tailor-made model, and not the roll-your-own model. Rollies were giveaways before the ban, but sold for $3 or more after the ban.

The value across different facilities did not vary a lot, but I would guess that state to state the base value changes, but the dollar for dollar exchange would not be affected.

It is also prudent to note, that the higher security level of the facility, the higher the price was for contraband, including tobacco once it was banned.
